- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecast tends to peak too early or too high after recent spikes in history, then drops sharply — suggesting overshoot and premature correction.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to anticipate gradual decline after peaks, often holding high values longer than observed.
- Lagged response to recent low prices: model delays correction, holding prices higher than true outcome when recent history shows downward trend.
- Forecast sensitivity to recent high values: if last 5–7 days are high, model overreacts with exaggerated high forecast — should dampen response to recent spikes.
- Model underestimates late-period (last 10–15 days) price drops, especially when true outcome shows sharp decline after mid-period peak.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trend linearly — true price often reverses or stabilizes after initial spike, not continuing trend.
- Adjust forecast downward if recent 5-day average is declining — model often ignores short-term mean reversion.
- Don’t assume trend continues — if recent 3–5 days show volatility or reversal, reduce forecast confidence and lower target.
